title: P256 flipped grid: permanent tabled X's, random-step Y-chains, X-pair partial fractions and LD64B table lookups; fraction labels, G526 grouped early abort, SWP receiver hash join, LS64 transport

claims.statement: For the protected full-production P256 target, the cold classical algorithm in proof.md and supporting documents recovers the scalar with probability at least0.39 using expected total work at most49945666708372151580518371615979064365956 scalar instruction equivalents, below2^125.231699025896549 group units at C1000, after a disclosed run gate (proof.md section17: a fresh coin opens the run with probability K/2^64; run success at least0.62992), under the disclosed correction-tail heuristic H_T of proof.md section16; per-run work at most the disclosed worst case in proof.md section15. N=2^70 nodes, each with MX=1024 permanent points X=R_g+[a]P and G=526 groups of 1024 Y-chains Y=[c+u*s]P with random start c and random nonzero step s, u<L=261290786. Flipped grid (the idea of soispoke's secp256k1 7f4f73d0, our own P-256 design and code): each batch is one step of the group's 1024 chains against all 1024 X's; per-X and per-X-pair constants have 1 TiB tables of eight 32-bit windows read by BFI addressing and LD64B, so each X-pair's batch-inversion element (x(Y)-x1)(x(Y)-x2) is one table lookup with an exact branch-free fold, both inverses come from one partial-fraction split, and the label's y(X)*w product is a table lookup. Leaf labels are176-bit keys of the192-bit fraction floor(2^192*x/p), computed within[-21,12] by truncated products against per-Y and per-X fraction rows (proof.md section3, FRACTION_LABEL.md). The run executes the groups in lockstep (per-group hop1 slots of5*2^17 records; a resident receiver that appends each 40-byte record to one cumulative home record array and joins it at arrival (BFI head address, SWP head update) into hash chains keyed by K2 mod2^59 with in-record next words and uncapped walks; per-group resolution) and halts at the first group whose resolver confirms [x]P=Q (latched stop flag); the expectation charges each group's per-batch and per-record work (both leaf passes, the chain step and Y-entry preparation with all their tails, two fixed inverses and the driver per batch, emission, both hops including the receiver's append and hash insert) and its main-pair hash walks (history-conditional pair counting) times a Chen-Stein prefix non-stopping bound; same-batch walks, K2 verifications and defective walks are charged globally without that bound (a listing costs no more than the pointer test it replaces), the leaf passes' correction tails (three sites per incidence, worst12) by an unweighted global row at6 per incidence over all batches (H_T: each taken with probability at most1/2 except each batch's first forward multiply and final backward update, charged a further8 per batch; defective batches at12), and the per-group fixed work of all526 groups, the phase-4 stages, generation, sampling, the tables and X areas and all caps, failures, preprocessing, resolution (each capped source request regenerates its Y), verification, barriers, control and output at their worst case. Includes construction, the tables, capped failure costs, fixed block-window transport using FEAT_LS64 64-byte moves at the disclosed IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED locations of proof.md section4 (including the pair tables, batch entries and Y entries), hop1 transaction-bound ACK and hop2 DONE-flag completion (the receiver is charged 11 for every potential record; walks 4 per chain visit and 5 per K2 match (each runs the masked K3 test), by pair counting), hash-head zeroing by DC ZVA on256-byte blocks (DCZID_EL0.BS=6), resolution, verification and output. Instruction counts are executed by a64.py, which does not check encodability; every listing is assembled by clang (proof.md section3). Peak memory below2^136bytes; preprocessing below2^119units included; no advice or auxiliary powers. Analytical bound under the stated ideal-coin blocking-port machine, not production execution or formal certification.

experiments.purpose: Check the protected constants, the flipped-grid leaf kernels (both passes, chain step, Y-entry preparation, table build) against their bit-exact models, exact labels and exact count formulas including full-window flushes, the tail census, the grouped hash-chain transport replay, resolution and the exact E-ledger.
